508: \begin{proof}
509: Let $\bu=\Calg^{-1}\bq$.  Since
510: $s_{\Calg}^2=\bq^\top\bu=\|\bu\|_{\Calg}^2$,
511: \[
512:  \left|\bq^\top\tilde\bu-s_{\Calg}^2\right|
513:  =\left|\langle\bu,\tilde\bu-\bu\rangle_{\Calg}\right|
514:  \le\|\bu\|_{\Calg}\|\tilde\bu-\bu\|_{\Calg}
515:  \le\varepsilon s_{\Calg}^2.
516: \]
517: This proves the pointwise two-sided quadratic-form comparison.  Dividing its
518: lower side by $1-\varepsilon$ gives upper validity for this query, while
519: combining both sides gives the displayed sharpness factor.  Applying the lower
520: inequality actionwise on the simultaneous family event gives the all-domain
521: upper condition; only the played query uses the upper inequality for
522: sharpness.  For PCG the argument is unchanged once the certificate is expressed
523: in the original $\Calg$-energy norm.
524: \end{proof}

526: Neither \Cref{lem:inverse-quadratic-certificate-new} nor
527: \Cref{cor:cg-interface-new} turns an ordinary floating-point residual into a
528: verified enclosure.  Literal numerical certification requires interval
529: arithmetic, directed rounding with derived norm bounds, or another verified
530: residual enclosure.  Float64 point checks remain engineering diagnostics.

532: Pointwise algebra alone is insufficient when a certificate uses fresh
533: randomness or is checked after a provisional action is chosen.  The following
534: accounting states when those events are measurable and how their failure
535: probabilities combine.
536: 
537: \subsection{Measurability, randomized certificates, and edge cases}
538: 
539: Let $\mathcal J$ be a finite or countable certificate-source index set.  For
540: $j\in\mathcal J$, choose an $\cHist_t^-$-measurable failure budget
541: $\delta_{j,t}$ before drawing its random object.  Let $\mathcal P_{j,t}$ be the
542: pre-reward sigma-algebra immediately before that draw.  It may equal
543: $\cHist_t^-$ for a round-start draw or include the selected action and earlier
544: randomness for a post-selection check.  It is sufficient that
545: \[
546:  \Pr(\mathcal E_{j,t}^c\mid\mathcal P_{j,t})\le\delta_{j,t},
547:  \qquad
548:  \sum_{j\in\mathcal J}\sum_{t=1}^T\delta_{j,t}
549:  \le\delta_{\rm cert}\quad\text{almost surely}.
550: \]
551: The tower property and a union bound give simultaneous validity at least
552: $1-\delta_{\rm cert}$ without independence.  Countability makes the joint
553: event measurable, the nonnegative double sum well-defined, and the union bound
554: valid.  On an uncountable score domain,
555: the solver upper event must already be simultaneous.  A pointwise certificate
556: cannot be union-bounded after adaptive selection unless it is separately
557: verified at the selected action with the correct conditioning.
558: Realized terminal spectral quantities may be used for post-hoc analysis, but
559: they cannot be inserted into an earlier action-time radius unless a predictable
560: prefix envelope was supplied at that time.
561: 
562: The logarithmic theorem remains correct for finite $\bar D_t\ge1$, but an
563: exponentially large factor can be vacuous.  Rotating ill-conditioned metrics
564: can have large path length even with fixed eigenvalues; conversely, a closed
565: path can have positive length and equal endpoints.  The endpoint Thompson
566: distance ignores the selected path.  The Thompson-Finsler length of the
567: selected direct SPD path is factorization-independent, whereas a factor-path
568: upper bound depends on the chosen factorization and interpolation.
569: For data-dependent Fisher weights, an explicit absolutely continuous factor is
570: required: a singular principal square root need not be differentiable.  A
571: uniform positive spectral floor is essential; positive damping supplies it
572: automatically.
